videos.t: CLIP ft. Ranieri Spina - Tour de First
videos.desc:
CLIP ft. Ranieri Spina - Tour de First

Footage taken from the CLIP's 'Tour de First' performance at Firstsite, Colchester part of their 'museums at night' on Thursday 26th October. Our performance moved through the building, beginning in the vast opening foyer and finishing in the the enclosed gallery spaces, exploring how the acoustics change along the way and the everyday sounds would expect to hear within each space.

videos.t: Electromagnetic Fields of Clacton Arcades
videos.desc:
What do arcade lights sound like? I toured a number of Arcades in Clacton, Essex with cinematographer Jamie Weston to uncover the hidden sounds. 

All electrical equipment produces a magnetic fields, and when you stick a wire coil into a magnetic field, the coil induces a current proportional to the field's strength and when amplified, we can hear this current.

Listen to my soundscape of Coastal Arcades on BBC Sounds here: http://www.frazermerrick.com/portfolio/hidden-sounds-of-coastal-arcades/

videos.t: DIY Solar Panel Microphone
videos.desc:
Super happy with this first prototype instrument, which makes sound from light! The solar panel generates current as the photos from the bike light hit it...which we then hear as sound.

This unit is actually already sold, but I’ve already got ideas for v2...stereo with two panels perhaps?! Special thanks to my old man for guiding me with the machining, my first time trepanning!

FYI the noise at the start is the light from the lamp I’m using...it sounds best in the dark 😅

videos.t: Listening to light with a solar panel microphone
videos.desc:
From light up dog collars to floating hot tub lights, I scoured eBay for a variety of battery powered lights to build this sample library of tones and textures. Download this sample pack: https://frazermerrick.bandcamp.com/album/led-solar-panel-sample-pack

When photons of light hit a solar panel a small electrical signal is generated due to the photovoltaic effect. And just like an audio signal from a microphone, when we amplify this signal, e.g connect to a speaker, we hear this signal as sound.

videos.t: Frazer Merrick - Pulsar (Solar Panel CV with the Volca Sample)
videos.desc:
Experimenting with the new setup, as well as listening to light I'm now using a second (smaller) solar panel to provide CV to the Volca Sample - the flashing of the red bicycle light becomes the tempo of the drum beat.

Also trying out my new DIY walkie talkie pedals, playing with how distances effects the degradation of the signal.
